title: It starts small.
paragraphs:
It starts small.
A laugh you shouldn’t entertain.
A voice you shouldn’t trust.
Then one day—you don’t recognize yourself.
“Bad company corrupts good manners.” — 1 Corinthians 15:33

That verse doesn’t whisper.
It warns.

Because corruption is rarely loud.
It’s subtle.
Comfortable.
Familiar.

You don’t fall overnight.
You drift.

A little compromise.
A little silence.
A little “it’s not that bad.”
Until your convictions start negotiating with your cravings.
But here’s what we miss…

The issue isn’t just who you’re with.
It’s who you’re becoming because of them.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Jesus didn’t die just to forgive your sins—
He died to break their influence.

Yes, He ate with sinners.
But He never let sinners rewrite His standards.

He carried truth into dark rooms—
He didn’t let darkness carry Him.
So ask yourself, warrior:

Are the people around you pulling you closer to Christ…
or making sin feel normal?

Because your environment will either fuel your calling
or slowly choke it.
But hear this—clear and burning:

You are not too far gone.
You are not too entangled.
You are not stuck in who you’ve been around.

In 2 Corinthians 5:17, Scripture declares:
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.”

New heart.
New direction.
New circle.

You may need to walk away from voices that feel like home—
just to return to the God who is your home.

Hard truth.
Holy freedom.
